newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr up as trade row fears ease, bourses climb.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr up as trade row fears ease, bourses climb.

text.p: A volatile dollar surged more than four yen in early trade on Thursday as a senior Japanese official soothed market fears over Washington-Tokyo trade friction and helped the U.S. currency claw back recent steep losses.
In equities, European bourses got off to a good start, led by Paris which climbed over 1.7 percent as anxiety faded over disruption of the timetable for the launch of the Europe's single currency.

Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, dubbed "Mr. Yen" for his influence on exchange rates, was again the oracle who sent markets into a spin with comments on currencies, interest rates and the trade balance.

After the dollar tumbled to a seven-month low against the yen on Wednesday, Sakakibara, director general of the Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said overnight that Japan would act "decisively" against excessive currency moves.

He added that the issue of U.S.-Japan trade relations was "being played up excessively" and that Japan's current account surpluses would not be a major topic of discussion when leaders of the biggest industrial nations meet next week in Denver.

Fears that the burgeoning Japanese surplus would cause trade tensions with Washington made the dollar slump to 110.70 yen on Wednesday. After Sakakibara's comments, the dollar rebounded to 114.20 in early European dealings.

"The reasons for the dollar coming off in the first place haven't changed just because of what Sakakibara said, but the wild swings we have seen mean people will now hold tight and see what the U.S. position is." said Austin White, the foreign exchange manager at Yamaichi.
Concern about a trade row grew after U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Wednesday Japan should avoid running up external surpluses that would hurt global growth.
"The U.S. and Japan are trying to firefight before it gets unmanageable," said Paul Meggyesi at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"You can expect to hear more backtracking on the trade front today."

The U.S. currency also strengthened against the mark amid hopes European Union countries will soon reach an accord on the budget deficit stability pact which requires them to observe fiscal discipline after they join economic and monetary union.

Expectations have grown that France, which asked on Monday for time to consider the issue, will soon agree to the pact. European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday he believed a deal would be reached at the EU summit in Amsterdam next week.
"The easing of the problems vis-a-vis the stability pact has seen people move out of marks," said White at Yamaichi.

The growing EMU optimism, coupled with a Wall Street's fourth consecutive record close on Wednesday, also boosted the Paris bourse, which suffered steep losses after the socialist victory in this month's election.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index climbed 1.7 percent to 2,746.19 points before falling back slightly by mid-morning.
"This rise is a little surprising with the Socialists in power but the market seems to not be taking this into account while it waits for the first policy measures," one trader said.

In Frankfurt, stocks also made healthy gains, helped by Wall Street and the stronger dollar, which is seen as helping German exporting businesses. But doubts on monetary union persisted and would limit gains, traders said.
"We are delighted to see the market getting back in step with Wall Street," said one dealer as the DAX index advanced by 0.74 percent in early dealings.
"But if we don't get a clear message from (Finance Minister Theo) Waigel and (Bundesbank President Hans) Tietmeyer today, this will still be a nervous market."

The Bundesbank is expected to discuss Waigel's controversial plans to revalue assets at its regular council meeting on Thursday. The idea caused a big row between Bonn and the central bank, which viewed an original proposal to use the revaluation proceeds to help Germany meet Maastricht deficit goals as unacceptable. London, Europe's biggest bourse, was the poorest performer, barely managing to show a profit by mid-morning after a series of strong rallies recently.
"I get the feeling that people are running out of trading ideas, but then they don't want to sell either," said one dealer. "I think we're in for a bit of consolidation."
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7240 marks and 114.16 yen compared with 1.7144 marks and 111.36 yen in late trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 5.9 points at 4,730.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 48.09 points at 2,744.28.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 32.73 at 3,710.16.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1030 GMT
Gold was fixed at $341.80 an ounce, compared with Wednesday's close of $344.05. Silver was down two cents at $4.75.
